description: Girls with a mission! 🚀 We’re an all-girls team exploring the Moon and Mars to tell the cute, heroic stories of NASA’s lonely, hard-working equipment left behind in space.
summary:
Beyond the Footprints is a free, browser-based interactive storytelling experience designed for school-aged space enthusiasts. Through a dreamlike journey across the Moon and Mars, users follow a rover along a trail to discover six pieces of NASA equipment left behind. At each checkpoint, they explore short videos, archival photographs and mission facts before collecting a memory to build their own personal museum. The experience is accessible through a single link, with no downloads or sign-up required, and works across desktops, tablets and mobile phones.

Combining imaginative storytelling, interactive exploration and educational content, the project brings NASA's historical space hardware and its scientific contributions to life, from lunar soil experiments to detecting marsquakes and achieving the first powered flight on another planet.

Although missions eventually end, their machines and discoveries remain valuable. Beyond the Footprint transforms forgotten hardware into pioneers of exploration, encouraging young learners to appreciate past achievements and develop curiosity about space science.

Left behind in the cosmic dust, yet forever alive in human memory.
details:
Beyond the Footprints is a browser game with six pages. Players fall asleep in a dream and pick the Moon or Mars. A rover drives along a dotted path to three numbered checkpoints on that planet. At each one, a short video plays and then an intro card appears with a badge, mission facts and archive photos with captions. Players press "Collect Memory" and the item joins their museum. The museum shows collected items in full colour and uncollected ones as grey silhouettes, and clicking a collected item opens its summary. After both planets, all six items glow together and the player wakes up in a sunrise bedroom. A progress badge such as "2/6" is always visible, and progress is saved so a refresh doesn't lose it.

⭐Benefits

  • It opens from one link, with no download or sign-up.
  • It is designed for desktop, tablet and phone.
  • Pacing is gentle, with locked checkpoints, short videos and bite-sized text.
  • Music can be switched off.

Intended impact we want school-aged space enthusiasts to learn what NASA's left-behind hardware did, such as testing the Moon's soil, finding marsquakes and flying on another planet. We also want them to see these machines as pioneers, not "space junk".

💻Tools and technology

  • HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript in a single file, with no framework
  • Inline SVG and CSS for all artwork and animation
  • The YouTube player for the videos, and the browser's saved storage for progress
  • Netlify for hosting
  • Kiro, an AI coding assistant, and an ordinary computer. No special hardware.
  • Gemini
  • ChatGPT
  • Eleven Labs Studio
  • Canva AI

Creativity The learning is wrapped in a dream story with a mysterious transmission. The watercolour look, a rover that follows a dotted trail, and a museum filled one memory at a time make exploring the reward, not reading. Each machine's story ends in a "left behind, never forgotten" message.

✅Factors we considered

  • Age-appropriate wording and a colourful, non-boring design
  • Accuracy of facts, for example we reworded one claim about the Lunar Roving Vehicle to "the first vehicle driven by astronauts on another world"
  • Accessibility: keyboard use, captions on photos and reduced-motion support
  • Easy access for judges and classrooms, with a permanent link and small files
  • Working on different screen sizes
